subject: pharmacology
title: Tapentadol, Methadone, Buprenorphine and Pentazocine: Atypical and Mixed Opioids

steps.tx: **Tapentadol** fuses mu agonism with noradrenaline reuptake inhibition in one molecule, aiming at mixed nociceptive and neuropathic pain with less constipation and nausea than equianalgesic oxycodone in trials (no serotonin arm separates it from tramadol, and no CYP2D6 lottery governs it: glucuronidation clears it directly). Seizure caution and serotonin syndrome warnings still attach through its monoamine action, and it is scheduled wherever misuse data demanded.
steps.say: Tapentadol is tramadol redesigned: direct mu action, noradrenaline only, no genetic lottery.

left.title: Tapentadol design
points: Mu agonism plus noradrenaline reuptake inhibition
Active as parent drug, glucuronidated directly
Neuropathic pain contribution from monoamine arm
Less gastrointestinal burden than oxycodone in trials

right.title: Tapentadol cautions
points: Serotonin syndrome with serotonergic partners
Seizure caution in predisposed patients
Controlled scheduling for misuse potential
Avoid with MAO inhibitors

steps.tx: **Methadone** is a racemic shapeshifter: mu agonist, NMDA antagonist and monoamine reuptake inhibitor with a half life averaging 24 hours but ranging tenfold between patients, making accumulation across the first week its defining danger. It serves opioid substitution therapy, complex and neuropathic cancer pain in specialist hands, and QT prolongation (torsades at higher doses and with interacting drugs) walks beside it. Induction deaths cluster in days 3 to 7 when yesterday's doses are still arriving.
steps.say: Methadone accumulates silently for a week and stretches the QT; induction is its killing season.

nodes.label: Long variable half life accumulates over days
Sedation peaks days 3 to 7, not day 1
Slow titration, ECG and interaction surveillance

steps.tx: **Methadone** is racemic and has three relevant actions: mu agonism, NMDA antagonism and inhibition of monoamine reuptake. The average half life is about 24 hours, but it varies about tenfold between people, so doses given on successive days pile up. That first week accumulation is the specific danger of induction, and deaths cluster on days 3 to 7 while earlier doses are still present. Uses are opioid substitution and, in specialist care, difficult cancer pain including neuropathic pain. QT prolongation and torsades accompany higher doses and interacting medicines.
steps.say: Methadone acts at mu receptors, blocks NMDA receptors and inhibits monoamine reuptake. Its half life averages a day but can be ten times longer in one person than another, so the drug stacks up during the first week. Induction deaths cluster on days 3 to 7. Higher doses and interacting drugs also lengthen the QT interval and can cause torsades.

vis.alt: A concentration curve shows methadone still accumulating through the first week, with sedation highest between day 3 and day 7.
vis.caption: Methadone level continues to rise across the first week of induction, and sedation is marked as peaking from day 3 to day 7. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Buprenorphine**, a partial mu agonist with fierce receptor affinity and slow dissociation, delivers analgesia with a ceiling on respiratory depression (though not on sedation with benzodiazepines aboard) and doubles as opioid substitution therapy sublingually, by depot injection and by patch. Its affinity lets it evict full agonists and precipitate withdrawal in dependent patients dosed too early, the induction choreography (wait for moderate withdrawal, COWS scored) that substitution clinics ritualise.
steps.say: Buprenorphine hugs the receptor hardest and activates it least; time its start to withdrawal or it causes it.

left.title: Partial agonist advantages
points: Ceiling on respiratory depression alone
Long duration: patches, depot and sublingual forms
Substitution therapy with lower overdose lethality
Analgesia adequate for moderate to severe pain

right.title: Partial agonist traps
points: Precipitates withdrawal if started too early
Blocks full agonist analgesia at high occupancy
Benzodiazepine co sedation removes the ceiling's comfort
Naloxone reversal needs higher, infused doses

steps.tx: **Pentazocine**, the ageing kappa agonist and mu partial antagonist, produces dysphoria and psychotomimetic effects through kappa receptors, raises cardiac work (unwelcome after infarction), and precipitates withdrawal in mu dependent patients while providing ceiling limited analgesia. Its historical pairing with antihistamines (the T's and blues abuse era) and skin fibrosis from chronic injection complete an adverse museum. Modern formularies retired it; examinations keep it as the kappa dysphoria archetype.
steps.say: Pentazocine is kappa's dysphoria made pharmaceutical: historically interesting, clinically retired.

left.title: Kappa agonism signature
points: Dysphoria, hallucinations and depersonalisation
Analgesia with a low ceiling
Miosis less reliable than mu agents
Cardiac stimulation: avoid after infarction

right.title: Mixed agonist antagonist rules
points: Precipitates withdrawal in mu dependence
Never layer onto full agonist therapy casually
Pentazocine, nalbuphine and butorphanol share the pattern
Chronic injection sites fibrose and ulcerate

steps.tx: **Substitution therapy** for opioid dependence rests on this lesson's pharmacology: methadone (full agonist, daily supervised then take home) and buprenorphine (partial agonist, safer ceiling, office based in many systems) both cut mortality by half or more versus no treatment, retain patients better at adequate doses, and are tapered only when stability argues, because relapse after detoxification, with tolerance lost, is the overdose epidemic's favourite mechanism.
steps.say: Methadone and buprenorphine halve dependence mortality; detox without them is the dangerous intervention.

nodes.label: Opioid dependence assessed with withdrawal scales
Buprenorphine in withdrawal, methadone titrated slowly
Taper only when stability and patient choice align

steps.tx: **Methadone's interaction web** punishes inattention in both directions: enzyme inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, efavirenz) plunge levels into withdrawal, inhibitors (azole antifungals, some SSRIs) push toward sedation and QT events, and its own QT effect stacks with antipsychotics, macrolides and hypokalaemia. ECG thresholds (QTc beyond 450 ms caution, beyond 500 act) and electrolyte care are protocol, not garnish, in substitution and pain services alike.
steps.say: Methadone levels swing with every inducer and inhibitor; the ECG is part of its prescription.

left.title: Levels falling (withdrawal)
points: Rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin induction
Efavirenz and nevirapine in HIV therapy
Pregnancy increases clearance in later trimesters
Split dosing sometimes required

right.title: Levels rising (toxicity)
points: Azole antifungals and fluvoxamine inhibition
QT stacking: antipsychotics, macrolides, low potassium
QTc beyond 500 ms demands dose action
Sedation review at every medication change

steps.tx: **Analgesic ceiling concepts** sort this lesson for examinations: full agonists (morphine, methadone, fentanyl) have no analgesic ceiling short of toxicity, partial agonists (buprenorphine) ceiling respiratory depression while analgesia largely persists at clinical doses, and mixed agonist antagonists (pentazocine, nalbuphine) ceiling analgesia itself early. Asking which ceiling a vignette describes, respiratory or analgesic, separates the three families faster than any structural recall.
steps.say: Name the ceiling: analgesia, respiration or both, and the opioid family names itself.

left.title: Ceiling taxonomy
points: Full agonists: no analgesic ceiling
Buprenorphine: respiratory ceiling, analgesia retained
Pentazocine class: early analgesic ceiling
Tramadol and tapentadol: ceilings set by seizures and syndrome

right.title: Clinical translations
points: Escalating cancer pain: full agonist territory
Dependence treatment: partial agonist safety exploited
Postoperative mixed agents largely historical
Ceilings vanish when sedatives combine

steps.tx: **Perioperative planning** for patients on these agents is a specialist choreography: buprenorphine continued (its analgesic contribution real, full agonists layered atop at higher doses), methadone baseline continued exactly with acute pain treated additionally, and never a mixed agonist antagonist introduced for postoperative pain in a dependent patient. Withdrawal prevention outranks theoretical receptor purity in every guideline, because uncontrolled pain plus withdrawal is the relapse recipe hospitals keep baking by accident.
steps.say: Continue the baseline opioid, treat acute pain on top, and keep mixed agents out of dependent patients.

nodes.label: Acute pain treated with layered full agonists
Addiction and pain teams co own the chart
